articles.title: GTA 6 Will Make Pro Athletes Perform Worse, NBA Star Says
articles.summary: Steven Adams of the NBA's Houston Rockets has predicted that all the major professional sports leagues will experience a dip in quality this November because top athletes will be too focused on GTA 6. Speaking to press, Adams said, "Look at the NFL, look at all the leagues, and watch them plummet.
body: He went on to say things should get back to normal after athletes finish the game. "It should come back up though; most of the boys will get it done. Hopefully they finish the game," he said.
Adams went on to say that other aspects of professional sports leagues will suffer, too, including coaching and scouting efforts that he said will be "horrendous," but "just for November."

Adams is obviously not being totally serious here, but GTA 6 is indeed one of the most highly anticipated game releases ever, and a lot of people--including pro athletes--are going to play it. We'll have to check back in November to see if athletes playing the game had any adverse effect on stats, however.
Before this, an NFL player blamed his on-field struggles on video games, while NFL QB Kyler Murray is known for playing too much Call of Duty.

articles.title: Nintendo Turns 137 Today, Making It Older (And Better) Than Sliced Bread
articles.summary: Nintendo is officially 137 years old today, and while that's an odd number to celebrate, it's certainly an impressive one. While it's a leading producer of video games and gaming hardware, the company originally started life as a maker of hanafuda playing cards in 1889, evolving with the times to…
body: That makes for a long list, but the biggest surprise, as pointed out online, is that Nintendo is literally older than sliced bread. Technically, this would make sliced bread the best thing since Nintendo, and for double-technicality points, we're referring to commercial pre-sliced bread. According to the history books, pre-sliced bread made its commercial debut 38 years later, on July 7, 1928, when the Missouri-based Chillicothe Baking Company began using Otto Frederick Rohwedder's bread-slicing machine to deliver tasty portions of the household staple to customers.

Today, Nintendo is worth many billions of dollars thanks to the release of several highly successful consoles, including the Wii and the Switch. In recent years, it has also intensified its efforts to be more than just a video game company, launching new theme parks and slowly releasing more feature film adaptations based on its original IP.
The two Super Mario Bros. movies developed by Illumination have each grossed north of $1 billion at the box office, and the next project is a live-action Legend of Zelda movie.

articles.title: Marvel Rivals Needs an Intervention
articles.summary: Poor balancing, toxic players, and a flawed approach to cosmetics have put Marvel Rivals in a bad place. It desperately needs an intervention to turn its troubles around.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Carlos Morales, who is a massive fan of Marvel whether it’s comics, movies, or video games. He’s sunk well over 1000 hours into Marvel Rivals.

These problems can’t be something that Marvel and Disney are too happy about, especially since Avengers: Doomsday, which is almost certain to be a financial success, is only a few short months away and could generate a large influx of new players. Let’s take a look at what’s gone wrong with Marvel Rivals, and what NetEase needs to do to turn things around.

These problems have been so pronounced that many players on social media have even called for Zhiyong, the game’s lead combat designer, to be fired. While that may be several steps too far, such sentiments don’t materialize in a vacuum, and they’re only exacerbated by the game’s other issues, many of which stem from the cosmetics.

articles.title: Xbox Mythic Achievement Will Be Microsoft's Version of a Platinum Trophy — And It Has an Extravagant Unlock Sound
articles.summary: Microsoft is expected to imminently launch Xbox Mythic Achievements, its own version of PlayStation's platinum Trophies, and you can now hear how they will sound when unlocked.
body: Xbox has previously confirmed plans to introduce its own method of tracking your full completion of a game — that is, when you have unlocked all of a title's 1,000 Gamerscore by nabbing every single Achievement.

Now, an update to the Xbox PC app has revealed the sound effect for an Xbox Mythic Achievement being unlocked, which has been discovered buried within the update's files. You can hear its rather majestic audio cue just below, courtesy of Xbox leaker Klobrille.

The sound is a suitably more grandiose version of the regular achievement unlock ping, which already can be heard in a more dramatic form when a rare achievement (owned by only a small percentage of players) is unlocked instead.

Microsoft's new Xbox Mythic Achievement effect is longer and more majestic still, lasting around 15 seconds as the audio wooshes in, builds, and then reverberates around. It's satisfying stuff, though whether it'll actually encourage you to grind for hours to get that full 1000G is entirely your choice.
points: Microsoft is expected to imminently launch Xbox Mythic Achievements, its own version of PlayStation's platinum Trophies, and you can now hear how they will sound when unlocked.

articles.title: Activision’s Halo Game: Everything We Know So Far
articles.summary: Microsoft is overhauling its Xbox business in a big--and painful--way. Part of the effort to "reset" Xbox involves enlisting Call of Duty publisher Activision to make the next Halo game.
body: Here's what we know about Activision's Halo game, and what comes next for Halo Studios.

The biggest question is what is the new Halo game from Activision? The announcement from Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty didn't reveal any specifics, but a story from The Hollywood Reporter said it is a "full-feature, mainline installment" in the long-running series.

Activision boss Rob Kostich said in a statement to Game File that Activision is trying to make the "greatest Halo game ever." He said the ambition is to make a game that is "worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place."

"It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community," he added.

articles.title: Diablo 5 Wants You To Feel Your Power, Not Just See A Bigger Number
articles.summary: Diablo 5 won't be out until 2029, but Blizzard is already sharing plenty of details on the game following its reveal at BlizzCon earlier this month. The power fantasy of being a demon-slaying warrior is one aspect of the Diablo experience that Blizzard wants to overhaul.
body: Speaking to PC Gamer, game director Joe Shely explained how players should feel and look more powerful as they level up. "Diablo is a game that, in many ways, is about your character getting stronger and when the monsters get stronger at the same time, especially outside of your control," game director Joe Shely said. "You've filled the experience bar, you get stronger, you should feel awesome now, a wave of light pulses out from you, a bunch of monsters die."

"That's wonderful, but then you're going to go hit some more monsters, and you should feel powerful. And sometimes automatic scaling can get in the way of that feeling, which is so core to it, and that's why this is a really important question. And so, we're going to take a somewhat different approach to that in Diablo 5."

In Diablo 4, the game was criticized for having an aggressive layer of level-scaling for enemies. Even if you'd optimized your loadout and equipped optimal skills, there was always that friction between the player and the world, with players pointing out that the diminishing returns on Paragon points and fewer gear upgrades resulted in a frustrating bottleneck for them.
points: Diablo 5 won't be out until 2029, but Blizzard is already sharing plenty of details on the game following its reveal at BlizzCon earlier this month.

articles.title: Sony PlayStation Patent Would Solve System Problems With AI Vibe-Coded Patches
articles.summary: Anyone who's had a console knows that on a long enough timeline they will have some kind of technical bug that you need to troubleshoot, and Sony is trying to get around that reality with an AI tech support agent.
body: Sony has filed a patent for an AI that would keep an eye on your system, looking for any kind of red flags, and then use an LLM to write up a patch for your system to either preemptively fix the issue or to send a report to engineers at Sony. The problem is, that unless you can turn this feature off, all the data processed on your PlayStation would potentially be visible to this agent. It would likely need total access to successfully monitor a system for any and all hardware and software issues.

It's also possible that the system could make small issues into much larger ones. As Patentlyze found, the patent says "an automated system sending repair instructions to a device in your living room needs careful guardrails so a small hiccup does not become a larger one." After all, the PlayStation 5 (and likely the PlayStation 6) are just specialized computers, and there have been plenty of times that I've broken something by fixing a small problem that I probably could have just ignored (or wasn't a real problem to begin with).

articles.title: Beloved cockney-orc Lord of the Rings games Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War finally make their way to Switch 2
articles.summary: As if this season wasn't packed enough with games to play, the acclaimed 'Nemesis system' Lord of the Rings games Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War finally come to Switch 2 later this month.
body: Set to launch on the console on the 30th September, both Lord of the Rings games boast all previously released DLC. Aspyr seems to have handled the conversions, and both games are available in a new bundle that you can pre-order for 50 percent off. Without the discount, the bundle sells for £62.99 / $70.

In Eurogamer's Shadow of Mordor review from 2015, Aoife Wilson - like so many other people - praised the game's procedural Nemesis system, whereby the game's enemies could level up after encounters with you and rise through their own ranks. This system helped make an otherwise passable open-world action games feel refreshing. Johnny Chiodini reviewed Shadow of War in 2017, but felt that improved gameplay was let down by a dreadful story.

The Nemesis system has remained a standout feature from the series. Aside from a few exceptions, like the Lich system in Warframe and maybe Watch Dogs: Legion 's NPC relationship system, few other games have implemented something similar. Perhaps that's because Warner Bros owns the patent until 2036.

articles.title: 'Toy Story 5' Now Officially Streaming on Disney Plus
articles.summary: After an excellent box office run, Pixar's Toy Story 5 just got a Disney Plus streaming release date.
body: After a standout run at the box office, Pixar’s latest animated film is now streaming on Disney Plus.

Toy Story 5 opened in theaters on June 19, overcoming potential sequel fatigue as it went on to gross over a billion dollars worldwide. Thus far, it has brought in more than $1.1 billion on a $250 million budget, making it the highest-grossing movie in the series' history and the third-highest-grossing film of the year (after Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey ).

While there was some understandable skepticism about Pixar releasing yet another Toy Story film, especially after Toy Story 4 seemed to wrap up many story arcs, the latest installment once again charmed critics and audiences. The film has a 93% critics’ score and a 94% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, with reviews praising its animation, performances, and humor. While Pixar’s output has been up and down in recent years, it still seems to bring its A-game for the series that put the studio on the map.

articles.title: Blizzard to take "a somewhat different approach" to level-scaling in Diablo 5, suggesting more influence from Diablo 2 than Diablo 4
articles.summary: Blizzard has hinted at yet another core mechanic in Diablo 5 seemingly inspired by Diablo 2. Notably, the in-development action-RPG will tackle level-scaling differently from the way it's done in Diablo 4.
body: Game director Joe Shely revealed - in a roundtable interview at BlizzCon (via PC Gamer ) - that Blizzard is aware of the desire to feel powerful in Diablo games, a feeling that the level-scaling system in Diablo 4 (and 3) somewhat betrays.

If you're unfamiliar, automatic level scaling is when enemies in a game's world keep pace with your own level. In other words, you're never going to run into an area where enemies out level you, but similarly you can't go back to the starting zone and feel how much more powerful you've become. This was the approach adopted by Diablos 3 and 4 - a somewhat controversial change from Diablo 2.

Said Shely: "Diablo is a game that, in many ways, is about your character getting stronger and when the monsters get stronger at the same time, especially outside of your control… You've filled the experience bar, you get stronger, you should feel awesome now: a wave of light pulses out from you, a bunch of monsters die."

"And sometimes automatic scaling can get in the way of that feeling," Shely added, "which is so core to it, and that's why this is a really important question. And so, we're going to take a somewhat different approach to that in Diablo 5."
points: Blizzard has hinted at yet another core mechanic in Diablo 5 seemingly inspired by Diablo 2.
Notably, the in-development action-RPG will tackle level-scaling differently from the way it's done in Diablo 4.

articles.title: Former Halo leaders lament effective closure of Halo Studios, as one employee finds themselves promoted and fired in same week
articles.summary: Former Halo leaders Bonnie Ross and Kiki Wolfkill have added their voices to the chorus of people wishing laid-off Halo Studios employees well after Microsoft's drastic downsizing of the studio yesterday.
body: The Xbox cuts were so sudden one former Halo Studios employee, cinematic director Josh Daniels, said he was promoted and then laid off in the same week. "Promoted and laid off in the same week is pretty wild," wrote Daniels on LinkedIn. "I'm one of the many hit by the Halo Studios layoffs."

Daniels' departure was a result of yesterday's Xbox cuts, which saw 268 people lose their jobs across a combination of Halo Studios, other unnamed first-party studios, and Xbox Game Studios management layers.

Halo Studios is reduced to a "small" support team as a result, with major Halo development moving to Activision, where a "purpose-built" team - separate from Call of Duty - has been created to develop "the next Halo title".

Bonnie Ross, the former head of Halo and founder of 343 Industries (which became Halo Studios), responded to yesterday's news on LinkedIn: "It was difficult to wake up to the news that the Halo Studio is essentially being shut down today, with only a small number of roles remaining," she wrote.

While the new Steam Machine, Steam Frame, and Steam Controller launched with little hype, that doesn't change how much of an impact this hardware should have had across the board.
With the Linux-based SteamOS as a solid replacement for Windows 11 and console-like PC gaming, Steam's hardware was meant to be the start of something great for PC gaming.
